newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says Iraq rejected 50,000-T sugar offer.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says Iraq rejected 50,000-T sugar offer.

text.p: Turkey's state sugar refineries Turkseker said on Thursday Iraq had rejected its offer of 50,000 tonnes of white sugar for $390 per tonne because Baghdad found the price too high, company General Manager Selahattin Hun said.
"Our offer was turned down by Iraq. They said the price was too high," Hun told Reuters.
He said the sugar would have had Baghdad delivery if accepted.
Turkey offered the sugar, whose quality was not specified, in December under a U.N. formula which allows Iraq to sell oil worth $2 billion to buy food and medicine.
Traders earlier said Iraq was evaluating about 120 offers from international sellers for supplies of two to four cargoes of low quality sugar of between 12,000 to 14,000 tonnes each.
Iraq is expected to buy about 300,000 tonnes of sugar in the six months of the U.N. deal.
